    feat(hybrid): skip restore of guest-unwritten config CSRs (ABI v6 write-mask)
    
    ResumeDriver now double-gates every mask-governed config CSR restore --
    the Andes scalars, PMA, the M-ext block, mcache_ctl/mmisc_ctl -- on caps
    (the ENGINE implements it) AND wm_live (the PRODUCER's guest actually
    wrote it, per hybrid_state_v1.write_mask). An untouched CSR is skipped
    entirely: its drained value is only the producer's reset default, which
    can legitimately differ from this RTL's reset value (msp_bound all-ones
    vs 0, milmb.IEN 0 vs 1), so skipping keeps the engine at its OWN reset
    state -- what real silicon would hold -- and makes producer/engine reset
    divergence harmless for every engine with no per-engine data upstream.
    
    HYBRID_FLAG_WRITE_MASK clear (a pre-v6 producer) falls back to the old
    restore-everything behavior, so existing flows are unchanged. The drain
    side stays full-width: re-reading is side-effect-free and records the
    engine's true exit values.
    
    Recording-bus tests cover both directions: with a mask only the written
    CSRs are restored (per-block and per-PMA-entry), and with the flag clear
    everything restores as before.

feat(hybrid): skip restore of guest-unwritten config CSRs (ABI v6)

ResumeDriver now double-gates every mask-governed config CSR restore -- the
Andes V5 scalars, PMA, the M-ext block, and mcache_ctl/mmisc_ctl -- on caps
(the engine implements the CSR) AND the new v6 write-mask (the producer's
guest actually wrote it). An untouched CSR is skipped entirely: its drained
value is only the producer's reset default, which can legitimately differ from
the consuming engine's own RTL reset value (msp_bound all-ones vs 0, milmb.IEN
0 vs 1), so leaving it unrestored keeps the engine at exactly what real silicon
of that engine would hold. This makes producer/engine reset divergence harmless
by construction, with no per-engine data flowing upstream into the producer.

The gate reads through a small wm_live() helper: when HYBRID_FLAG_WRITE_MASK is
clear (a pre-v6 producer file) it returns true for every slot, so the old
restore-everything behavior is preserved and existing flows are unchanged. The
drain side stays full-width, since re-reading is side-effect-free and records
the engine's true exit values.

This pins external/andesim_abi at v6 (write_mask[2] + hybrid/write_mask.h,
carved from reserved so the struct size is unchanged) and registers
tests/hybrid/write_mask.test.cpp with ctest. That test exercises the slot map,
the set/test helpers, and the CSR-write instruction decoder but was never wired
into the build in the old history, so it ran as an orphan; it now runs under
check. The resume_driver and state_abi contract tests gain the matching v6
sections.
